https://www.politico.eu/article/latvia-m.text: Latvian authorities have discovered a tunnel used by migrants to cross the border from Belarus illegally amid long-standing concerns that Minsk is weaponizing migration against the EU. On Monday, border guards detected 15 people who had come through a 10-meter-long tunnel near the border fence between Belarus and Latvia, Riga’s Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava said Tuesday. Belarusian ruler Alexander Lukashenko is a close ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin, and his regime has supported Moscow’s war of aggression against Ukraine and taken a hostile stance toward the EU. Advertisement Advertisement Tunnels have previously been found in Lithuania, according to Baltic media , but this is the first time one has been used to cross into Latvia. “This is the first case in which a tunnel has been used for illegal crossing of the state border into Latvia. No signs of violations had previously been detected in this exact location, and no detentions of persons illegally crossing the state border had occurred there,” Dombrava wrote on X . Authorities returned all 15 people to their “country of departure” and are continuing to inspect the area around the tunnel. Latvia launched an operation Tuesday to strengthen border security. Dombrava has described illegal border crossings from Belarus as a “hybrid threat.” Authorities have prevented more than 9,000 illegal attempts to cross the border from Belarus so far this year, the Latvian State Border Guard said in a press release .

https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.text: A German district court on Thursday issued an arrest warrant for far-right Alternative for Germany lawmaker Maximilian Krah over unpaid legal fees stemming from a dispute with comedian Jan Böhmermann, according to various German media outlets . In 2024, Böhmermann read out a listener’s letter on his podcast alleging that Krah, a former member of the European Parliament, had ordered 200 bottles of Champagne for an entire tent at Munich’s Oktoberfest. Krah denied the claims and called the story “complete nonsense.” Böhmermann later said that his research indicated the number of bottles was likely only 50. Krah, who had already been dubbed “ Schampus-Max ” (Champagne Max) in some German media outlets, filed an injunction against Böhmermann over the claims for violation of his “personality rights,” according to Germany’s Der Spiegel , but the case was dismissed in December 2024. Krah was then ordered to cover litigation costs — which he is alleged to have failed to pay in full. Advertisement Advertisement The outstanding amount is less than €300, reported Der Spiegel . A court bailiff applied for an arrest warrant in mid-July when the lawmaker did not appear for an asset disclosure appointment, according to the outlet. Krah has since said he was neither aware of the appointment nor the outstanding costs. The Bundestag would have to lift Krah’s parliamentary immunity in order for him to be detained. Böhmermann had previously made headlines for triggering a diplomatic crisis after he insulted Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in a poem in 2016. Böhmermann’s lawyer and Krah’s office did not respond to requests for comment by the time of publication. A spokesperson for the court did not confirm the arrest warrant, citing privacy concerns. https://www.politico.eu/article/raphael-.text: PARIS — Raphaël Glucksmann won France’s center-left primary on Sunday, securing the backing of the Socialist Party and its allies for next year’s presidential election, organizers said. Glucksmann, a member of the European Parliament, won the contest outright with over 66% of votes, beating Socialist Party leader Olivier Faure and three other candidates in the first round. More than 120,000 people voted Friday, Saturday and Sunday. The leader of the small center-left Place Publique party entered the contest as one of the favorites. He now emerges strengthened from the primary, with access to Socialist Party funds and having built a broader base for his candidacy. Advertisement Advertisement “This result expresses something strong: that a left that is faithful to its values can unite, govern and win,” the MEP wrote online . “We are here to win the presidential election: Turn the page on Macronism, stop the far right and change our lives,” he added. But Glucksmann, a staunch supporter of Ukraine and a critic of China, now faces a much greater challenge: how to beat the far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon. The head of the France Unbowed party is surging in the polls, with the latest Ifop survey giving him 14% to 17% support , compared to 11% for Glucksmann. In recent weeks, Glucksmann campaigned against forming an alliance with the far-left leader. Three other candidates ran in the primary, including former minister Ségolène Royal and lawmakers Jérôme Guedj and Emmanuel Maurel. Some 140,000 people were registered to vote in the primary — including, 80,000 who paid €15 to take part but weren’t members of any of the parties whose candidates were running — raising uncertainty over the outcome. The online voting platform was also targeted by a cyberattack shortly after opening, organizers said in a statement on Friday, but “was never disrupted” and “the integrity of the recorded votes has not been compromised.” Advertisement Advertisement
